title: Feature gate: kernel auto-selection v2 + runtime config plumbing (env/region/model scoped)
author: Benji Okafor
content:
Title: Feature gate: kernel auto-selection v2 + runtime config plumbing (env/region/model scoped)

Summary
This PR adds the feature gating + configuration plumbing needed to enable Kernel Auto-selection v2 in a controlled, reversible way. The gate supports scoping by environment, region, and model identifier, and is wired into the runtime config loader with hot-reload support. This is intentionally “plumbing-only”: selection logic remains unchanged here; the runtime will continue to use v1 unless the gate evaluates to enabled for a given request/model.

Motivation
Kernel auto-selection v2 is expected to improve p95/p99 and stabilize throughput across heterogeneous GPU fleets, but rollout needs to be staged and quickly reversible (especially for Dedicated/Private deployments with constrained SKU options). We need consistent controls across Hosted, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments, with a clear precedence hierarchy between static runtime config and control-plane delivered policy.

What’s included
- New runtime config surface: kernel_selection.v2_gate
  - enabled: boolean (global default)
  - environments: allow/deny list (strings like prod/staging/dev)
  - regions: allow/deny list (e.g. us-east-1, eu-west-1)
  - models: allow/deny list (exact model IDs as surfaced by the model registry, e.g. llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2026-01-15)
  - mode: off | canary | on (canary is a strict allowlist-only mode; see below)
- Gate evaluation helper in runtime: GateEvaluator::kernel_selection_v2(request_ctx, model_id) -> (enabled, reason)
  - reason is a low-cardinality enum used for telemetry/debugging (e.g. DISABLED_GLOBAL, ALLOWED_MODEL, DENIED_REGION, ENV_NOT_ALLOWED, CONTROL_PLANE_OVERRIDE).
- Config precedence rules (documented in code comments + tests):
  1) Hard safety overrides (future hooks; currently none in this PR)
  2) Control-plane provided runtime policy (if present)
  3) Static runtime config file
  4) Default = disabled
- Hot reload integration
  - Gate config is part of the runtime’s dynamic config bundle; changes apply without restart where supported (Hosted/Dedicated).
  - Private deployments can still use static config only (control-plane bundle optional), but the schema is the same.
- Canary mode semantics
  - mode=canary enforces that only explicit model allowlist entries can enable v2 (even if enabled=true). This prevents accidental “global on” when config is shared across multiple fleets.
- Minimal telemetry plumbing
  - Adds a counter and structured log fields (no per-model cardinality in metrics):
    - runtime.kernel_selection_v2_gate.enabled (0/1)
    - runtime.kernel_selection_v2_gate.reason (enum tag)
  - NOTE: detailed per-request selection telemetry is handled in ENG-4824 / PR-28466.

Out of scope
- Kernel selection v2 decision logic (PR-28411/28452/etc.)
- Per-request candidate/feature emission (PR-28466)
- Deterministic replay harness additions (PR-28473)

Implementation details
- Adds KernelSelectionV2GateConfig to runtime/config/schema, with serde validation ensuring: (a) mode is one of off/canary/on, (b) allow/deny lists are normalized (trim/lowercase where applicable), (c) denylist takes precedence over allowlist within the same dimension.
- Request context wiring uses existing fields for env + region from the runtime context; model_id comes from the resolved model version after routing/pinning.
- Gate evaluation is deterministic and pure (no time/randomness); output is stable given the same inputs and config snapshot.

Testing
- Unit tests for config parsing/validation:
  - rejects unknown mode
  - normalizes region strings
  - denylist precedence
- Unit tests for gate evaluation matrix:
  - env-only allow
  - region deny
  - model allow + canary mode
  - control-plane override precedence
- Integration-ish test for dynamic config reload

Docs/Notes
- Added inline schema documentation in runtime/config/README (short section).
- ADR reference: ADR-017 kernel auto-selection v2 features and fallbacks (gate/fallback strategy aligns with “default off + staged allowlist”).

Rollout plan
- Default is disabled everywhere.
- Initial canary will be enabled via control-plane policy for a small model allowlist in one Hosted region (separate change).

Commits
1) config: add KernelSelectionV2GateConfig schema + validation
2) runtime: wire gate into config loader + dynamic config bundle
3) runtime: add GateEvaluator + tests for env/region/model scoping
4) observability: add low-cardinality gate metrics + log fields

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/config/schema/*
- runtime/config/loader/*
- runtime/kernel_selection/gates/*
- runtime/telemetry/metrics/*
- tests/runtime_config/*

Selected snippet
- Gate evaluation (simplified):
  enabled = cfg.enabled
  if cfg.mode == CANARY and model_id not in allow_models => return disabled(reason=CANARY_REQUIRES_MODEL_ALLOWLIST)
  if env in deny_envs || region in deny_regions || model_id in deny_models => return disabled(reason=DENYLIST_MATCH)
  if allowlists are present and no allowlist matched => return disabled(reason=NOT_ALLOWED)
  return enabled(reason=ALLOWED)

Review conversation
- Jordan Lee (requested changes): “Please make the reason string low-cardinality; do not include model_id/region directly as tags.”
  - Benji: Updated to enum reason; moved model_id to debug logs only (not metric tags).
- Michael Nguyen (requested changes): “Config precedence needs to be explicit; we’ve been burned by static vs dynamic confusion.”
  - Benji: Added precedence comment block + tests asserting control-plane override wins.
- Noah Patel (requested changes): “Canary mode should not allow global enable via enabled=true; require explicit model allowlist.”
  - Benji: Implemented canary semantics as described; added test.
- Ethan Park (approve): “Matches control-plane gate expectations; we can now drive rollout centrally per region/model.”
- Marissa Cole (approve): “Good rollback story. Please ensure docs mention default off + canary semantics.”
  - Benji: Added short README section.
